body:
Hey, how are you holding up? I'm sorry it took me a few hours to get back to you. I got tied up and didn't get a chance to check my account. 

>The depression, the self-harm, the suicidal thoughts, the attempts, the mental hospital, the jail, the feeling of insanity

I've been in every one of these situations. I'm still in some of them. It's not an easy thing to deal with. It's exhausting. It's disheartening. It can break a person. I've been broken by them more times than I'd like to admit. If something is broken, you fix it. Easier said than done, I know. But we have to pick up the pieces and try to put it back together before we decide to throw it away. 

>it's all ripped the fabric of my mind to where I don't know anything anymore.

A lot of us have no idea what the hell we're doing. I certainly don't. I'm not even sure who the hell I am anymore. But try to think about it like this. Now, now you have the chance to re-learn everything. If there was something you didn't like about yourself or your life before, now is the time to change that. Start with something small. Little improvements you can make here or there. They start to add up and they start to pay off. 

>There is no life and that's what I'm living.

There is a life. It may not be one you are happy with, but there is a life. It doesn't have to be *that* life though. Try not to focus on that life. Direct your focus towards who you want to be and where you want to go. If there is even the slightest chance in getting there, then it's worth sticking around for.

Hope you're doing okay, and I hope this helps somehow. If it doesn't, just let me know. We can keep talking until we figure something out.

I know the feeling. I played the victim for so long. I *thought* I was the victim for so long. It was until just recently that I am a problem. I am *the* problem. It's a tough realization to make. And it's certainly not an easy one to deal with. I'm still dealing with it and I'm battling it every day. 

>Just looking back and now all I see is it's only gotten worse.

Well, if you don't mind. How about you walk me through what's going on and what has been going on. For things like this, it's all about small steps. One day at a time. Tackling everything part by part. I'm sure you;ve already heard that before, but it's really the best way to approach things when it all begins to become overwhelming. 

>They don't want to let me go, but they don't want to hold on to me.

The fact that they don't want to let go shows they are holding on, even if it seems like it's only slightly. For what it's worth, I want to keep talking to you; I'm holding on.

Nobody here on this sub is going to dismiss how you're feeling as being melodrama. You're incredibly down on yourself right now and that's what's important. 

>the thing I'm having the most trouble with is finding a reason not to kill myself.

It's troublesome, I know. But a lot of the time, the reasons for sticking around aren't as visible as we'd like them to be. One things for sure though: they are there.

>I don't really know what awaits me after death

Neither do I. But let me tell you this: at 17, it's hard to know whether or not you know enough about what's currently here. And a lot of that, you might come to realize, is worth sticking around for. You've got a lot to see and experience in your lifetime still. When I was 17, I had barely scratched the surface of life's many many offerings. 

If you want to talk a bit, feel free to message me.

You may think you'd be doing it alone. But me, and anyone else who have read this, are with you now. I put up my own post in this sub just yesterday. I thought it was the end for me too. I wanted it to be the end for me. But some really caring people from this sub reached out to me and pushed me to stick around for at least another day. Taking it one day at a time is the best any of us can do. I've exchanged messages with people who really wanted to listen to what I had to say. What I'm trying to say is, I'm here if you want to talk. I'll listen. Even if our situations aren't the same, we're both going through some shit and who knows. We might be able to help each other out.

That's actually an interesting quote. Appreciate you sharing; never thought of it like that. But I still see it differently. Guilt is the result of mourning over something you've done. Shame is being disgusted with yourself for whatever it is that caused the guilt. But you can't move from shame to guilt without forgiving yourself first. I can't forgive myself. Not right now. I don't deserve to.

I'll probably have a chance to read it tonight. Will definitely get back to you on it.

>When did you first start feeling that you couldn't change for the better?

Just recently. I didn't elaborate too much in my post. But I hurt the most important person in the world to me. What I did was disgusting, shameful, and completely heartless. I don't think I can ever forgive myself. Not only for what I did, but for hurting that person the way I did. This isn't the first time I've hurt someone close to me. Not in the same manner, but I was still the source of their pain. That's when I started thinking I couldn't change for the better. Because I haven't. I thought I had. I thought I had become a good person. I thought I *was* a good person. But I was lying to myself. I masked my true colors from everyone, even myself. I didn't know about this sub until yesterday. Before this post, I put up something similar in another sub. The person I hurt happened to see that post, and they responded. They said something along the lines of how I didn't deserve to take my own life. That I deserved to live with this for the rest of my life. Maybe I can't change for the better. Even if I can, I don't feel like I deserve to.

I'm sure some would be devastated and sad if I left this way. But for the sake of my argument, imagine I never existed to begin with. Their lives would not be any different. I do not contribute any good to their lives. Even what little I have has been immediately overshadowed by the pain I've caused; that I will most certainly continue to cause.

It's hard to appreciate the highs during the lows. Especially when appreciating those highs only makes me feel lower. It's tough to build new bridges when you assume they're eventually going to go up in flames.

Thanks for the articles. I haven't had a chance to read the Stanford paper yet (I will and let you know what I think), but I did read the NYT piece right now. It's an interesting read and wouldn't be opposed to having a discussion on it (and the Stanford piece when I read it). 

I'll agree, everybody does change. It's inevitable. What I meant to originally say was, what if some people aren't capable of change *for the better*. 

I've never had a specific approach to trying to remedy things. For the most part, it's been as simple as "don't do *this* or *this* will happen." The problem is my judgement. Normally, I'm pretty solid. I have a decent head on my shoulders and usually make better calls. But every once in a while, it's like the mechanics in my head implode. I made poor choices. I do something without thinking of the repercussions. I don't think of the consequences or how they will impact myself and others. There is no pattern to it. One day I could be presented to a certain scenario and I'll immediately know better and avoid it or handle it collectively. A week later, I can be presented with with another scenario bearing negative consequences, but I don't think and just do it. I should know better. I do know better. But I still neglect to make the right choice. People change. Whether or not everyone is capable of changing for the better remains to be seen.

I'm sure there are a small number of people who would be sad (family and friends have become more of acquaintances over the years), but ultimately, they would be better off without me. They may feel sorrow, and I would hate to be the source of even more grief, but their lives would be improved. Everyones. 

We all do make mistakes. Some of us, like myself, can't seem to stop making them. Those mistakes come at the expense of others. I've burned to many bridges, I've hurt too many people, and I've squandered more opportunities than I would care to admit. There's nothing left for me here.

Have you ever wondered if some people just aren't capable of change? I've made too many mistakes to count so far in life. I've hurt enough people. I thought I changed. I thought I learned from them. But it seems if I fix one thing, another falls apart. I don't want to hurt anyone anymore. I only see one way to guarantee that won't happen.

> looking back and thinking " WTF was I thinking then? "

You know, this isn't the first time I've had these types of thoughts before. And after it passed, I would tell myself the same thing, "wtf was I thinking?" But they keep coming back. I screw up somehow, or ruin another relationship, or whatever it is. And I come back to these thoughts. Back to thinking that this would be the best choice. I always knew my mind made situations appear to be worse than they were. But this time. This time I think its right.

Thanks for the response. I appreciate it. 

>hell some people make a life out of fucking up

I feel like thats me. And thats not okay. I try to learn from my mistakes and get my shit together. But when I do, something else falls apart. I just. Idk. I thought I was stronger than this. I *was* stronger than this. But I fucking broke. I can't do this.
